tools.name: screen_numbers
tools.description: Screen UK phone numbers against the TPS and CTPS registers before calling. Each result is clean, tps-listed, ctps-listed, unknown, suppressed or consented. A live key draws prepaid UK credits (one per distinct valid number); a test key returns fixtures at no cost. Same as POST /v1/screen.

tools.name: wash_au_numbers
tools.description: Wash Australian phone numbers against the Do Not Call Register. Live key only (the register has no test mode). One prepaid AU wash per distinct valid number; invalid numbers cost nothing and numbers the register gave no answer for are refunded. Same as POST /v1/dncr.

tools.name: check_dead_numbers
tools.description: Live mobile network (HLR) lookups: whether each mobile is live, switched off or dead. Live key only. One prepaid dead number check per mobile, two for a US number; numbers that are not mobiles and invalid numbers cost nothing. Same as POST /v1/dead-number.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: The calling key and its account: environment, scopes, company name and whether one is still required (GET /v1/me), plus the UK credits left (GET /v1/usage), the Australian washes left (GET /v1/dncr) and the dead number checks left (GET /v1/dead-number). findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "screen_numbers" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "buy_credits" is 1677 chars, far longer than this server's median (311). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_dead_numbers · Private data: set_company_name · Public sink: screen_numbers, wash_au_numbers, check_dead_numbers.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_dead_numbers · Private data: set_company_name · Public sink: screen_numbers, wash_au_numbers, check_dead_numbers

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
